pitfalls.title: Passing degrees to Math.sin / Math.cos
pitfalls.description: Math.sin and Math.cos strictly accept radians. Supplying degrees (e.g. 90 instead of Math.PI / 2) silently distorts angular spacing, producing a mangled or broken shape.
pitfalls.badSnippet:
// Passing raw degrees silently produces incorrect geometry
const angle = i * 45; // 45 degrees, wrong
pitfalls.goodSnippet:
// Always convert angles to radians (radians = degrees * Math.PI / 180)
const angle = i * (Math.PI / 4); // radians

pitfalls.title: Omitting ctx.closePath()
pitfalls.description: Failing to invoke closePath() before stroke() leaves the path open between the final vertex and the initial vertex, creating a visible seam in the stroke outline.

seniorInterviewTip: For 60fps animations, precompute sin/cos values in a lookup table or move vertex computation into a vertex shader — Math.sin/Math.cos are transcendental and expensive in hot loops.
